findings.summary: The stated cause of the vmapped read's 54 ms is refuted by the record's own control: the paragraph at :48-55 says placing the decision inside the mapped function is what the batch paid for, yet the vmap-carried arm, which has no conditional inside or outside the map, costs 54.65 ms at one slice against 54.36 ms with the conditional and 2.07 ms for read_batch on the same state and device, so removing the conditional changes nothing and the placement of the decision cannot be the cost. What the control actually shows is that jax.vmap over read is slow for a reason the node did not identify (the nested vmap in stationary_stencil's _inside_cells pass, or the traced control flow in fixed_points.solve, are the candidates), and the brief's item (1) asked for the cause to be confirmed. The walls, the per-lane flags and the delivered read_batch are unaffected, so this does not hold the node; the explanatory paragraph should state that the cause is narrowed to vmapping read itself and remains unidentified, and the identification belongs in a followup, because §3 and §4 will batch this route and will otherwise carry a wrong explanation forward.

The plan's done-when for this section requires the record to table kernel launches and host-device copy bytes per call, and the record tables neither: the profiler returned zero device events and the record reports that as an instrument fault with the 54 ms arm as its positive control, which is the right way to report a failed instrument but still leaves the done-when clause unmeasured. Copy bytes are asserted zero by construction rather than measured. The per-slice wall carries the bound, so this does not hold the node; the profiler fault should be recorded as a followup so §2's done-when is visibly still short of one clause rather than silently narrowed.

The section's bound is at most 0.2 ms per slice batched over sixteen or more slices; at sixteen the measured wall is 0.230 ms, a 15 percent miss, and only sixty-four slices meet it, so §2's done-when is not satisfied as written. The brief anticipated a miss and required the remainder to be attributed by stage, and the record instead decomposes the four points arithmetically into a 2.14 ms per-call share and a 0.0998 ms per-slice floor, which is an attribution by regression and not by stage; the 0.73 ms by which the batch's per-call cost exceeds the single read's is named but not resolved. This does not hold the node because the brief admits the miss and the number is reported honestly, but §2's done-when is unclosed and the stage attribution it asked for is missing.

_rebuilt_reading at :312-321 is a verbatim copy of the rebuild closure left in read at :279-287, so the two whole-mesh rebuild paths can drift and a change to field_from_jets' call signature must be made twice; read should call the new helper instead of keeping its own copy. Nothing is wrong at runtime today and the gate exercises both paths, so this does not hold the node.

The measurement's mixed-state arm reports rebuild_fraction 0.0 at every batch size because the certificate's converged and trial states resolve the same cells, so logs/measure.log never exercises the reload branch of the lax.cond at :392; the only evidence that the batch-uniform rebuild branch works is the gate's forced stale-cell test. The record says this explicitly, so it is not a hidden gap, but a measured rebuild-branch wall is still absent even though the plan asks for one ('a rebuild step's wall').
